summary: ansible-core 2.16 breaking changes: plugins taking timeout from the cli entry now honour lower-precedence configured values, ansible-test container test plugins can no longer reuse running containers, and the service module no longer sets permanent OpenBSD flags on enable/disable.
questions: My connection plugin timeout changed after upgrading, why?
Can ansible-test reuse an already running container?
Why doesn't the service module keep my OpenBSD rc flags anymore?

answer_card.title: ansible-core 2.16 breaking changes
answer_card.answer_md:
- Plugins using the config system with a `cli` entry for `timeout` now pick up values configured via lower-precedence methods. If you relied on `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT`, add the overlapping config entries to your plugin.
- **ansible-test**: container-based test plugins no longer reuse running containers.
- **service** on **OpenBSD**: enable/disable no longer writes permanent variables/flags; manage those separately (e.g. an `rcctl` config task).
